shared_elements: quadruped animal shown in profile facing right
horizontal band of repeated motifs running above the figural field
circular disc motif (rosettes in A, small round element in B)
animal head with clearly marked eye and muzzle in profile
figural field framed/divided by straight incised lines
justification: The most specific correspondence is structural: in both, a strip of small repeated units (rosettes in A, arch-like knobs and vertical hatching in B) runs horizontally above a field containing profile animals, with straight incised lines separating band from figure. The biggest difference is manner and finish: A is a smooth, precisely modelled shallow relief on a flat dressed wall with naturalistic anatomy and human attendants, whereas B is a rough, rounded, schematic carving on the irregular faces of a free-standing block with stacked, disjointed creatures and no coherent single scene.
